The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on the interval $[-1,5].$ The graph of $y={f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above. It consists  of two line segments and the arc of the semicircle centered at $(4,0)$ with radius $1.$ Find $f(4)$ if $f(-1)=2\pi .$
question.worked_solution:
From the fundamental theorem of calculus, we find that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =f(4)-f(-1) \\ {\int }_{-1}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =f(4)-2\pi  \\ f(4) & ={\int }_{-4}^{1}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x+2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Remember that the integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis.

The graph consists of $2$ parts: two line segments for $x\in [-1,3]$ and the arc of a quarter-circle for $x\in [3,4].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-1}^{3}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The first integral ${A}_{1}$ represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,3].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+4)\cdot 2 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

The second integral ${A}_{2}$ represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,4].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot (1)^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of the original integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{4}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =5+\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the value of the integral, we can find $f(4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) & ={\int }_{-4}^{1}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x+2\pi  \\  & =5+\frac{\pi }{4}+2\pi  \\  & =5+\frac{9\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
